html:
Rongorongo is a system of glyphs carved on wooden tablets from Rapa Nui, first reported by a missionary in 1864. About two dozen objects carrying it survive, scattered in museums, and no one has deciphered it.

The glyphs show birds, people, fish and plants, in lines that turn over at each end. Scholars still argue whether it is true writing, and whether it arose before or after the islanders saw Spanish writing in 1770.

If it is writing made on the island, it is one of the very few independent inventions of writing, with cuneiform, Chinese and Maya script. Knowledge of it was lost after the slave raids.
